clue.text: Girl has business in south of France

parts.note: Mona is a girl's name
CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A young woman runs her company down on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins the two pieces and 'in' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The principality sits on the Mediterranean coast, enclosed by southern French territory.

clue.text: Tenant perhaps-what he pays to hold a party

indicators.note: one thing holding another means the second goes inside the first

parts.note: a tenant pays rent to the landlord
a side is one party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A tenant's rent money goes on throwing a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a celebration but here means one side in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a property, such as one who rents it, is a dweller there; 'perhaps' marks the tenant as one example.

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry about why selfless people do anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally: an unselfish person acts for the sake of virtue, not gain.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfless person acts purely out of virtue; and the same phrase is an exasperated exclamation like 'honestly!'.

explanation.surface: A small sprig of foliage offered in place of a handbill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A small leaf is a little piece of foliage; a flyer is a printed handbill given out.

explanation.surface: A question whether a salad vegetable has been gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' means composed and calm, not gathered; the salad sense reads the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means utterly calm and composed, and literally describes a chilled salad vegetable.

explanation.surface: A two-word note telling someone to flavour food thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a verb for flavouring and 'well' an adverb; both are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: One time of year follows winter; and a natural source of water rising from the ground is a well.

explanation.surface: A stronghold set aside for the country's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A peel is a small fortified tower house on the Anglo-Scottish border; Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive tower house of the border country, and the Victorian-era premier who founded the Metropolitan Police.

clue.text: Anticipation that weed will absorb phosphorus

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to hoe is to weed with a garden tool
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: An expectation that a weed will take up phosphorus from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' looks like a noun (a plant) but is the verb to hoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectation of something wished for is a synonym.

indicators.note: reciting is speaking out loud, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: being obliged to someone is owing them

explanation.surface: Someone was made to recite a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric verse addressed to a subject is a type of poem.

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large
prey is the victim of a hunter

explanation.surface: A bird's huge kill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish hawk is a bird of prey.

clue.text: Dying for cigarette, having to contain outcry

indicators.note: one piece containing another wraps around it

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
a din is a loud noise or clamour

explanation.surface: A smoker desperate for a cigarette has to stifle a scream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dying for' reads as craving; the definition is just 'Dying', with 'for' a link. FAG is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Waning or growing weaker towards extinction is a fading away.

clue.text: Story wrongly held back as liable to be wrong

indicators.note: one piece holding another keeps it inside

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

indicators.note: back means the word for wrongly runs right to left

parts.note: ill can mean badly or wrongly, as in ill-advised

explanation.surface: A story is misheld as libellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' is a synonym piece, not an anagram signal; 'back' turns it and 'held' puts it inside the story word. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of making mistakes, human and imperfect.

explanation.surface: A marksman's advice doubling as a call for modesty.
explanation.walkthrough: A rifleman literally lowers the aiming device on the gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling for smaller goals; and a marksman adjusting aim down by moving the aiming device.

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Panic as a gun is drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like panic but means a hanging tab.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab or loose hanging piece of material, like a label tied on.

explanation.surface: Splitting a capital city as a kind of divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means of the head: a line in the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A line dividing hair on the head, and a separation of a couple.

clue.text: Role in Othello I missed in past

indicators.note: missed means the letter is left out

parts.note: Iago is the villain in Shakespeare's Othello

explanation.surface: An actor missed a role in Othello in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Back in time, previously: 'years before now'.

clue.text: Quantity of land about to be enclosed in a prison

indicators.note: enclosed in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a cage is a prison, with 'a' giving A
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A plot of land about to be fenced off as a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Area measured in units of 4,840 square yards each.

clue.text: Point to characteristic aim of French revolutionaries

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
a quality is a characteristic trait

explanation.surface: Pointing out a trait typical of French rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the pieces. Liberté, égalité, fraternité was the French Revolution's slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Égalité, the second word of the French revolutionary motto.

indicators.note: beside places the railway after the establishing word

parts.note: to found is to establish

explanation.surface: Setting up a steelworks beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A works where metal is cast is a casting shop for iron.

clue.text: Circus lion loose awful risk of encounter on this

indicators.note: awful suggests these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A circus lion on the loose poses an awful risk to anyone who meets it.
explanation.definitionFit: A path heading towards a crash is one where a meeting impact is likely.

indicators.note: before places the relaxed word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: limp means slack or relaxed
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone loosened up before their mind cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent, as of water, or lucid prose.

indicators.note: translated means the letters are changed into another form

explanation.surface: A Tibetan phrase rendered in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tibetan' is a noun here: a person of Himalayan Tibetan stock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan people famous as mountain guides are of Tibetan origin.

indicators.note: wounded suggests damage that leaves the letters disordered

explanation.surface: A wounded spearman says 'hard cheese' to bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard cheese' reads as British slang for bad luck, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Parmigiano is a hard grating cheese.

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary leader

explanation.surface: Yearning for a revolutionary figurehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the definition; 'Long' is a verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or pine for something.

clue.text: Hammer film seen at shopping centre

indicators.note: seen at puts the film beside the shopping centre, after it

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A horror film from the Hammer studio showing at the mall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' evokes the British horror film studio, but here it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden-headed hammer used in carpentry or croquet.

explanation.surface: Being scared of one's therapist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil or flinch is to show fear; a head doctor is slang for a psychiatrist.

indicators.note: a call is a spoken word, so the next word is heard

parts.note: wry means bitterly ironic

explanation.surface: Ordering bitter in a pub but getting whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like the beer but means sardonic.
explanation.definitionFit: American whiskey distilled mainly from that grain.

parts.note: top means the best
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest sun helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for a pith helmet worn in tropical heat.
